L41: Species: Dog
L42: 
L43: Area of Study: Medical Oncology
L44: Purpose of Study: The purpose of this study is to provide a direct comparison between the outcomes for dogs with peripheral T cell lymphoma (PTCL) treated with CHOP or LOPP chemotherapy. The findings of this study could help veterinarians understand if one protocol is truly superior to the other for dogs with PTCL.
L45: 
L46: In this study, your dog will be randomly selected to receive either CHOP or LOPP chemotherapy. At each visit, their lymph node size, blood work, and overall wellbeing will be assessed.
L47: Timeline: Both protocols involve treatments every 7–14 days and take 4-6 months to complete. Following protocol completion, your pet will return once monthly to assess remission status.
L48: 
L49: Eligibility: Your dog may qualify if:
L50:   * Confirmed peripheral T cell lymphoma diagnosis via cytology or histopathology
L51:     * No indolent forms of lymphoma, such as T zone lymphoma
L52:     * Cutaneous lymphoma will not be included
L53:   * No prior chemotherapy or radiation therapy for lymphoma. It is preferred that patients are not started on steroids in advance of enrollment. However, if deemed by the overseeing clinician, patients can still be enrolled on steroids for up to 10 days.
L54:   * No major lab work abnormalities that prevent chemotherapy administration
L55:   * No evidence of dilated cardiomyopathy, ventricular arrhythmia, or liver failure
L56: ## T Cell Diagnostic Testing
L57: 
L58: A diagnosis of T cell lymphoma can be made using one or more of the following tests:
L59: 
L60:   * Immunocytochemistry (ICC)*
L61:   * Immunohistochemistry (IHC)*
L62:   * PCR for antigen receptor rearrangements (PARR)*
L63:   * Flow cytometry
L64: 
L65: *Available through the 【12†MSU Veterinary Diagnostic Laboratory†vdl.msu.edu】
L66: 
L67: Client Benefits: This is a partially funded trial.
L68:   * A test must be conducted to confirm the T cell lymphoma diagnosis in study participants. T cell diagnostic testing can be conducted at MSU or through clients’ primary care veterinarians. Diagnostic testing at MSU costs approximately $250. For dogs accepted to the study, the cost will be reimbursed by an account credit at the MSU Veterinary Medical Center at trial completion (either when the protocol is completed or the patient develops progressive disease).
L69:   * Initial evaluation appointments will be charged. For dogs accepted to the study, recheck exams during clinical trial appointments will be free of cost ($60 value per visit). Costs associated with blood work and treatment will remain the responsibility of the client (with the exception described below).
L70:   * Dogs will receive the first dose of doxorubicin (for those assigned to the CHOP protocol) or lomustine (for those assigned to the LOPP protocol) free of cost. First-dose administrative and blood work fees also will be free of cost.
L71:   * Clients are financially responsible for all treatments and diagnostics that are unrelated to the study.
L72: Client Responsibilities:
L73:   * To administer prednisone, chemotherapy, or supplemental medications as prescribed by the attending veterinarian.
L74:   * To comply with the visit schedule outlined by study investigators
L75:   * To report any abnormal behavior or signs of illness to study investigators.
L76:   * To contact study investigators if your dog is evaluated by any other veterinarians during the course of the study.
L77:   * To inform study investigators of any non-study-related veterinary treatments recommended for your dog during the course of the study.
L78: Contact Information: Please feel free to contact our Medical Oncology Team at (517) 353-5420 or cvm.oncoinfo@msu.edu to refer a patient or for any additional information. Referring veterinarian and client calls are welcome.

L80: Practitioners of interest: Primary care and specialty clinics, especially oncology specialties, in Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, Canada, and surrounding areas.

L54: #### ​Purpose of Study
L55: Immunotherapy, engaging the power of the immune system against cancer, has become a standard part of oncology care. One such approach utilizes the STimulator of INterferon Genes (STING) pathway. Our colleagues at University of Michigan, led by Dr. James Moon, have developed a drug that activates the STING pathway. This drug, called CMP-002, has been shown to combat cancer in a laboratory setting, with and without the use of another modulator of immune system, PD-1 blockade.
L56: This success prompted a collaboration with Michigan State University College of Veterinary Medicine as we hope to contribute to efforts that can help veterinary oncology patients and humans alike. Our initial studies, led by Dr. Vilma Yuzbasiyan-Gurkan at MSU, established the dose range tolerated in healthy dogs.
L57: The purpose of this study is to confirm the best dose of CMP-002 with or without PD-1 blockade for tumor-bearing dogs. CMP-002 has already been tested in healthy dogs. It is not uncommon for patients with cancer to process drugs differently, which is why we intend to confirm the best dose for tumor-bearing dogs. The findings of this study will then be used in future studies assessing the anti-cancer properties of CMP-002 with or without PD-1 blockade.
L58: #### Eligibility Criteria
L59:   * Inclusion criteria:
L60:     * Confirmed diagnosis of soft tissue sarcoma, lymphoma, osteosarcoma, histiocytic sarcoma, or malignant melanoma via cytology or histopathology.
L61:     * Visible tumor at the time of enrollment.
L62:     * Adequate organ function indicated by standard laboratory tests.
L63:     * Minimum weight requirement of 5 kg (11 lbs).
L64:   * Exclusion criteria:
L65:     * Prior anti-cancer treatment, including steroids, within 7 days.
L66:     * Indolent forms of lymphoma, such as T zone lymphoma.
L67:     * Expected survival < 4 weeks with treatment.
L68: #### Eligibility Diagnostics
L69: 
L70: Prior to study entry, pet owners will be charged an initial consultation fee and be financially responsible and required to have the following diagnostics performed in their dog:
L71: 
L72:   1. Diagnosis of select tumor type, if not already documented
L73:   2. Screening blood work and urinalysis, if not performed within 7 days
L74: #### Treatment
L75: The first group of patients (6–9 dogs) will receive CMP-002 alone. Their tumor will be measured and they will receive the CMP-002 infusion. They will then be observed overnight and blood samples will be taken at set timepoints. The dogs will visit their primary veterinarians one week later for blood sampling. Three weeks after the first treatment, the dogs will return to the MSU Veterinary Medical Center for a second infusion.
L76: Depending on previous response, they may be hospitalized again or sent home the same day. If tolerated, these treatments can be repeated every 3 weeks for a set number of cycles. Tumor biopsy samples may be collected at various timepoints.
L77: The second group of dogs (6–9 dogs) will receive CMP-002 with PD-1 blockade. Their tumor will measured and they will receive the CMP-002 infusion. They will then be observed overnight and blood samples will be taken at set timepoints. The dogs will return one week later for tumor measurements, blood sampling, and anti-PD-1 infusion. Three weeks after the first treatment, the dogs will return to the MSU Veterinary Medical Center for a second CMP-002 infusion.
L78: Depending on previous response, they may be hospitalized again or sent home the same day. If tolerated, these treatments can be repeated every 3 weeks for a set number of cycles. Tumor biopsy samples may be collected at various timepoints.
L79: #### Compensation
L80:   * This is a funded trial. All tests and treatments associated with the trial will be covered once a dog is enrolled.
L81:   * Complications associated with the trial will be covered. Clients are financially responsible for all treatments and diagnostics that are unrelated to the trial. Association between complications and trial treatment will be determined by the overseeing clinician and investigators.
L82:   * Initial evaluation appointments will be charged. For dogs accepted to the study, recheck exams during clinical trial appointments will be free of cost ($60 value per visit).
L83:   * CMP-002 (and PD-1 blockade, if included) treatment will be administered free of cost. Hospitalization immediately after CMP-002 administration and associated treatments will be free of cost. Blood sampling and tumor biopsies associated with the trial will be free of cost.

L53: Clinical Study: Time to Maximal Response to Neoadjuvant Corticosteroids in Dogs with Mast Cell Tumors
L54: 
L55: Purpose of Study:
L56: Mast cell tumors (MCT) are the most common skin tumor in dogs. MCTs can be treated in a variety of ways, with surgery being a common component of care. When MCTs are located in a challenging surgical location, we will try pre-treating with drugs to shrink the tumor and give the surgeon more flexibility. Historically, these pre-surgical treatments include chemotherapy and/or corticosteroids. Anecdotally, if the MCT shrinks, the effect only lasts for a limited period.
L57: To date, there are no studies identifying the ideal time between starting steroids and performing surgery. In this study, we plan to identify canine patients with cutaneous MCTs, administer corticosteroids, and before proceeding to surgery, clients (pet owners) will obtain daily measurements.
L58: The aim of this study is to identify guidelines for pre-operative steroid treatment with secondary goals of decreasing surgical risks and improving post-operative outcomes in dogs affected by this disease. Identifying an ideal pre-surgical treatment window can improve veterinarian confidence in surgical scheduling, help facilitate successful surgery, and limit the influence of steroids on wound healing.
L59: 
L60: Eligibility Criteria:
L61:   * Inclusion criteria:
L62:     * Confirmed mast cell tumor diagnosis via cytology or histopathology (may be completed through primary veterinarian or at MSU)
L63:     * Cutaneous mast cell tumor located on the trunk (above the elbow or knee)
L64:     * Mast cell tumor measures between 2-6cm in one dimension
L65:     * Bloodwork confirming adequate organ function and ability to undergo general anesthesia (may be completed through primary veterinarian or at MSU)
L66:   * Exclusion criteria:
L67:     * Prior anti-cancer treatment, including steroids, within 7 days
L68:     * Patients on NSAIDs need 5 or more days of washout before enrolling
L69:     * Evidence of MCT metastasis
L70:     * Expected survival < 4 weeks with treatment
L71:     * Diabetes mellitus or other systemic condition that interferes with safe steroid administration
L72: Eligibility Diagnostics:
L73: 
L74: Prior to study entry, pet owners will be responsible for an initial consultation at MSU and to complete the following diagnostics for their dog:
L75: 
L76:   * Cytology or histopathology of tumor in question to confirm diagnosis of MCT (if not already completed)
L77:   * Bloodwork ensuring adequate organ function to undergo general anesthesia (if not already completed)
L78: Staging diagnostics including abdominal ultrasound with cytologic evaluation of regional lymph nodes, spleen, and/or liver will be contingent on a overseeing clinician’s recommendation as well as client election. This is not a requirement for inclusion.
L79: 
L80: Treatment:
L81: Initial caliper measurements of the tumor will be obtained by 2 trained staff members on the day of enrollment. Clients will be trained by MSU staff in caliper usage and each dog will be prescribed prednisone, diphenhydramine, and either famotidine or omeprazole for 14 days.
L82: Each morning, the clients will obtain caliper measurements of the MCT in the 3 planes as instructed per specific training images. Photographs that include the caliper will be emailed to the primary investigators daily. In-person evaluations will be completed at MSU on days 7 and 14 to confirm measurement accuracy and allow for surgical planning.
L83: Surgical resection will be planned for Day 14 (+/- 1 day) with the MSU Soft Tissue Surgery service, and tissue will be submitted for biopsy analysis. Patients who experience significant or rapid tumor shrinkage may undergo surgery sooner.
L84: 
L85: If at any time throughout treatment, the tumor grows by >20%, the patient will be removed from the trial and given appropriate care based on clinician discretion.
L86:

L89:     * Up to 50% of the surgical fees and the histopathology fees will be covered
L90:     * All trial-specific medications (prednisone, diphenhydramine, famotidine/omeprazole) will be covered once enrolled
L91:     * Calipers will be provided
L92:   * If additional surgery is completed under the same anesthetic event, the client will be financially responsible

L46:   * Male or female felines, any age, any breed

L48: #### Exclusion Criteria
L49: 
L50:   * Feline with underlying health issues that put it at risk for anesthetic procedure:

L54: #### Background
L55: 
L56: In felines, the eye is the most common location for melanocytic tumors to occur. Unfortunately, melanomas have the potential to metastasize to other organs. Currently, there is no non-invasive diagnostic technique to differentiate ocular melanocytic tumors. Enucleation and histopathology are currently the only reliable technique to accurately diagnose feline iris melanocytic tumors.
L57: This study aims to explore the diagnostic utility of a novel imaging system to characterize spectral features of melanocytic tumors. It is hypothesized that high resolution imaging of iridial melanocytic tumors in felines will generate unique spectral data that will permit clear differentiation between malignant (melanoma) and benign (melanosis) regions using this imaging system.

L55: Purpose of the study:
L56: Histiocytic sarcoma is an aggressive cancer in dogs that often does not respond well to standard treatments like chemotherapy or radiation. While some dogs experience benefits, these treatments affect many cells at once and cannot adapt as a tumor changes. New research shows that cancer closely interacts with the immune system and surrounding tissues, suggesting that better treatments may need to work inside cells, not just target them from the outside.
L57: Quasiorganelle therapy is an experimental approach that aims to do this by using weakened, non-disease-causing bacteria derived from Listeria monocytogenes to deliver helpful genetic instructions directly into immune and tumor cells, with the goal of improving how the body recognizes and responds to cancer.
L58: The aim of this study is to determine whether quasiorganelle therapy can be given safely to dogs with histiocytic sarcoma and to determine an appropriate dosing schedule. The treatment has been tested in laboratory and preclinical studies but not yet in dogs with naturally-occurring cancer. Because animals with cancer may respond differently than healthy animals, this study also looks for early biological or clinical signs that the therapy may be beneficial.
L59: 
L60: Inclusion criteria:
L61:   * Confirmed diagnosis of histiocytic sarcoma, including hemophagocytic histiocytic sarcoma, as determined by immune marker expression.
L62:   * Visible tumor at the time of enrollment.
L63:     * Up to 5 lesions
L64:     * Sum of the longest lesion dimensions <15cm
L65:   * Adequate organ function indicated by standard laboratory tests.
L66:   * Minimum weight requirement of 20 kg (44 lbs).
L67:   * VCOG performance status up to 2.
L68: 
L69: Exclusion criteria:
L70:   * Concurrent diseases such as: diabetes mellitus, Addison’s disease (hypoadrenocorticism), Cushing’s disease (hyperadrenocorticism), kidney disease
L71:   * Active wounds.
L72:   * Concurrent medications such as: immunosuppressants (including corticosteroids, cyclosporine, azathioprine, mycophenolate) or systemic antibiotics within 14 days.
L73:   * Neutropenia, immunodeficiency, or immune-mediated disease
L74:   * Prior anti-cancer treatment
L75:     * Corticosteroid (prednisone) within 7 days.
L76:     * Chemotherapy within 14 days.
L77:     * Radiation therapy within 30 days.
L78: Treatment:
L79: The first group (8 dogs) will receive quasiorganelle therapy alone. Their tumor will be measured and they will receive the quasiorganelle infusion. They will then be observed for up 4 days at the MSU Veterinary Medical Center and blood and fecal samples will be taken at set timepoints. The dogs will return for treatment once weekly for 4 doses followed by 2 weeks off. This schedule will then be repeated two more times for a total of 16 weeks of treatment.
L80: Imaging to determine alterations in tumor size will be repeated at the end of each 4 week treatment period.
L81: The second group (8 dogs) will receive quaisorganelle therapy that includes gene therapy. Their treatment and monitoring schedule will be identical to that of the first group.
L82: 
L83: Following the 16 week treatment period, dogs will return for evaluation every 4 weeks or until progressive disease is documented.
L84: 
L85: Please note: While enrolled, dogs should not live with anyone who is pregnant or planning to become pregnant.
L86:

L88:   * This is a funded trial. All tests and treatments associated with the trial will be covered once a dog is enrolled.
L89:   * Complications associated with the trial will be covered. Clients are financially responsible for all treatments and diagnostics that are unrelated to the trial. Association between complications and trial treatment will be determined by the overseeing clinician and investigators.
L90:   * Initial evaluation appointments will be charged.
L91:   * Quasiorganelle therapy (with or without gene therapy) will be administered free of cost. Hospitalization immediately following administration and associated treatments will be free of cost. Blood and fecal sampling and imaging studies associated with the trial will be free of cost.
